blocks.text: Status Report: Management Buyout Advisory for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}

To Joseph Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Blankenship Inc. From Thomas Mccoy, Advisory Associate, for the deal team of Richard Mccoy, Partner, and Angela Cole, Analyst. Circulation is limited to the people named here. Some of the lender material below reached us under confidentiality letters, so please do not forward this report to the lenders or to anyone on the sellers' side.
We brought four decisions to you and the management group this period. You have made two of them. The other two remain open, and both now stand between the current drafts and a signing set.

You selected the senior lender whose final terms gave the company the most covenant headroom, although its pricing was not the lowest on offer. You also agreed that the sellers' note will rank behind the senior debt on the terms that lender asked for. That cleared the last open point in its commitment letter.

The first open decision is how the management equity divides among the members of the management group. The total contribution is settled. The individual amounts are not, and the subscription documents cannot be drafted until they are.

The second is who bears the transaction bonuses for staff outside the management group: the company at closing, or the sellers out of their proceeds. The answer moves the working capital figure, so the purchase agreement cannot go back to the sellers' counsel without it.

items: Senior debt. The lender you selected delivered its signed commitment letter, and its counsel circulated a first draft of the credit agreement within the week. The commitment carries the covenant package and conditions you approved, and the lender added nothing when it signed.

Financing structure. With that letter in hand, the structure described in our engagement letter is complete: {{fact:f:E-2018-001.scope}}, each now backed by a signed commitment. No source has been added or dropped along the way.

Lender process. Marketing of the debt is closed, and the final count stands at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.pipeline-lenders-approached}}. Each lender that declined has been asked in writing to return or destroy the information memorandum, and Angela Cole is logging the confirmations as they come back.

Valuation support. Angela Cole refreshed the analysis of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.comparators}} for the company's results through the latest month end. The agreed price still falls inside the range that analysis supports. She has marked the transactions whose figures come from press reports rather than filings, so the reader can weigh them accordingly.

Forecast model. Angela Cole rolled the model forward for the latest monthly results and re-ran the lender's covenant cases. Each case still passes at every test date, with the narrowest margin in the second year.

Lender diligence. The senior lender's accountants have finished their fieldwork. Their last questions, on inventory costing, were answered from the company's own monthly schedules, and nothing in their draft report bears on the commitment.

Credit agreement. We are checking the covenant definitions in the first draft against the model, so that the defined terms measure what management has actually been forecasting. Our comments go to the lender's counsel early next week.

Subordination agreement. The lender's counsel is preparing the agreement between the senior lender and the holders of the sellers' note. We will confirm that it reflects the ranking you agreed and nothing beyond it.

Purchase agreement. Your counsel and the sellers' counsel are on their third turn of the draft. Apart from the bonus question above, the one open business point is the length of the sellers' non-compete, which Richard Mccoy is taking up directly with the sellers' counsel.

Funds flow. Angela Cole is building the funds flow memorandum from the commitment papers. Until the payoff letter from the company's existing bank arrives, she is marking each figure in it as either final or estimated.
Equity documents. Your counsel has the subscription agreement in near final form and is holding the individual schedules until the split is agreed. Nothing else in those documents is open.
Closing checklist. I keep the master list of conditions, documents, and signatories. It goes to both sets of counsel each Monday, and only to them.

blocks.text: What the coming weeks depend on

Most of all, they depend on your two open answers. With them, the purchase agreement and the subscription documents can be finished together and checked against a single closing checklist. We would like both answers by the end of next week, so that counsel can spend the holiday weeks drafting on settled points.

They also depend on the lender's counsel returning the credit agreement promptly after our comments, and on the existing bank issuing its payoff letter. Neither is in our hands. If either one slips, we will tell you the same day.

Nothing this period has added to the fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}} set in our engagement letter, and we do not expect the closing work to change it. The next report will follow when the signing set is complete.
